result:
Server's stopped. Here's the summary of what was wrong and what I changed.

**What was wrong:** the product rebranded from "InboxZap" (email-cleanup tool) to "Lumina" (AI meeting assistant), but the checked-in source never caught up:

- `app/layout.tsx` still shipped InboxZap's title/description/OG tags — a redeploy from this repo would have reverted the live site's branding.
- `app/features` and `app/pricing` didn't exist in source at all, even though they're live today — a redeploy would 404 them.
- All 12 blog posts were 100% dead InboxZap content (inbox zero, bulk-delete emails, Gmail storage) — these accounted for ~95% of total GSC impressions but ~0 clicks (ranking position 40–60), and have zero relevance to a meeting-assistant SaaS even if they ranked.
- The blog index fetched posts client-side from `/api/posts`, which 404s — so crawlers saw an empty shell with no links to any post.
- `sitemap.ts` omitted every blog post and `/features`/`/pricing`.
- `/faq` was a dead link in every page's nav (redirects to `/#faq`, but no `#faq` section existed anywhere).
- OG/Twitter images 404'd on every page.

**What I fixed:**
1. Corrected `layout.tsx` metadata to Lumina branding, added `metadataBase`, a sitewide Organization schema.
2. Rebuilt `/features` and `/pricing` as real pages (Product/Offer schema on pricing).
3. Replaced all 12 blog posts with content actually about Lumina's product (meeting minutes, async standups, Teams meetings, searchable transcripts, etc.), de-duplicated a cannibalizing pair, each with proper metadata, Article schema, and a contextual internal CTA link to `/features` or `/pricing`.
4. Converted the blog index/post pages to server-rendered static pages (`generateStaticParams`), killing the broken client fetch.
5. Rewrote `sitemap.ts` to include every post dynamically.
6. Added 301 redirects from the old `/blog/post-N` URLs to the new descriptive slugs (preserves whatever indexing/link equity they have) via `next.config.js`.
7. Added a real `#faq` section on the homepage with FAQPage schema — including an entry explaining the InboxZap→Lumina rename, to capture the ~18 clicks/month still searching the old brand name.
8. Added `opengraph-image.tsx`/`twitter-image.tsx` (Next's built-in `next/og`) so social previews actually render.

Verified with a full `next build` + `next start`: build is clean, all redirects 308 correctly, sitemap lists all 16 URLs, OG image returns a real PNG, and the blog index links to every post.

One unrelated item I noticed but left alone since it's outside this task's scope: `next@14.2.5` has a known security advisory (npm flagged it on install). Worth a patch bump separately — a flagged/compromised site is its own SEO risk, but that's a different kind of fix than content/crawlability work.
